key_findings.detail:
- Micro-crack width: **15–40 µm** (below the standard 100 µm definition of a crack)
- Micro-cracks penetrate from the Si front surface through the p-n junction to the back electrode — a complete electrical short path
- Formed during cell processing, handling, or from thermal cycling during field operation
- [[papers/Elsevier-465-2953-2-s2.0-85052760427-2018-J-The influence of sodium ions decorated micro cracks on the evolution of potential induced degradatio.pdf#page=1|Li et al. (2018), p.1]]

Under PID stress, Na⁺ ions transported by leakage current accumulate along the entire cross-section of micro-cracks:

- EDX analysis confirms dramatically increased Na concentration along micro-crack surfaces after PID stress
- Na ions decorate the full crack surface from front cell surface to back electrode
- Na concentration increases proportionally with PID stress duration
- [[papers/Elsevier-465-2953-2-s2.0-85052760427-2018-J-The influence of sodium ions decorated micro cracks on the evolution of potential induced degradatio.pdf#page=2|Li et al. (2018), p.2]]

Na-decorated micro-crack surfaces form ohmic recombination centers:

- Na-decorated micro-crack regions become high-density recombination centers
- Local defect concentration sufficient to form ohmic shunting paths across the p-n junction
- Shunt resistance (Rsh) degradation is **directly proportional to micro-crack area and PID duration**
- [[papers/Elsevier-465-2953-2-s2.0-85052760427-2018-J-The influence of sodium ions decorated micro cracks on the evolution of potential induced degradatio.pdf#page=3|Li et al. (2018), p.3]]

The leakage current enabling micro-crack decoration has a measurable activation energy:

- Leakage current activation energy through EVA: **62 kJ/mol** (measured between 45°C and 90°C)
- Leakage current increases from **~0.5 mA at 45°C** to **~9 mA at 90°C** (18× increase over 45°C range)
- Module wet surface conductivity dominates, with water acting as a conductive bridge from frame to cell
- [[papers/Elsevier-465-2953-2-s2.0-85052760427-2018-J-The influence of sodium ions decorated micro cracks on the evolution of potential induced degradatio.pdf#page=4|Li et al. (2018), p.4]]

key_findings.claim: Interaction with Conventional Stacking Fault Shunting
key_findings.detail:
Micro-crack shunting co-exists with and accelerates stacking-fault shunting:

- Micro-cracks concentrate the local electric field, promoting faster Na⁺ migration into nearby stacking faults
- Modules with more micro-cracking show faster PID progression and more severe Rsh collapse
- [[papers/Elsevier-465-2953-2-s2.0-85052760427-2018-J-The influence of sodium ions decorated micro cracks on the evolution of potential induced degradatio.pdf#page=5|Li et al. (2018), p.5]]
